traits.smithy.api#documentation:
This is the Amazon EC2 Instance Connect API Reference. It provides descriptions, syntax, and usage examples for each of the actions for Amazon EC2 Instance Connect. Amazon EC2 Instance Connect enables system administrators to publish one-time use SSH public keys to EC2, providing users a simple and secure way to connect to their instances.

To view the Amazon EC2 Instance Connect content in the Amazon EC2 User Guide, see Connect to your Linux instance using EC2 Instance Connect.

For Amazon EC2 APIs, see the Amazon EC2 API Reference.

Region.documentation: The AWS region used to dispatch the request.

UseDualStack.documentation: When true, use the dual-stack endpoint. If the configured endpoint does not support dual-stack, dispatching the request MAY return an error.

UseFIPS.documentation: When true, send this request to the FIPS-compliant regional endpoint. If the configured endpoint does not have a FIPS compliant endpoint, dispatching the request will return an error.

Endpoint.documentation: Override the endpoint used to send this request

Pushes an SSH public key to the specified EC2 instance for use by the specified user. The key remains for 60 seconds. For more information, see Connect to your Linux instance using EC2 Instance Connect in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

smithy.api#examples.title: To push an SSH key to an EC2 instance
smithy.api#examples.documentation: The following example pushes a sample SSH public key to the EC2 instance i-abcd1234 in AZ us-west-2b for use by the instance OS user ec2-user.

The ID of the request. Please provide this ID when contacting AWS Support for assistance.

Pushes an SSH public key to the specified EC2 instance. The key remains for 60 seconds, which gives you 60 seconds to establish a serial console connection to the instance using SSH. For more information, see EC2 Serial Console in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.
The ID of the EC2 instance.

The public key material. To use the public key, you must have the matching private key. For information about the supported key formats and lengths, see Requirements for key pairs in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

The serial port of the EC2 instance. Currently only port 0 is supported.

Default: 0
The ID of the request. Please provide this ID when contacting AWS Support for assistance.
